datasets.title: Satellite-detected water extents in Mananjary District, Vatovavy Fitovinany Region, Madagascar as of 27 February 2022
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: TC20220221MDG This map illustrates satellite-detected surface waters in Mananjary district, Vatovavy Fitovinany region, Madagascar as observed from a Sentinel-1 image acquired on 27 February 2022 at 05:12 local time. Within the analyzed area of about 200 km2, about 6 km2 of lands appear to be flooded. Based on Worldpop population data and the detected surface waters, about 200 people are potentially exposed or living close to flooded areas. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT). Important note: Flood analysis from radar images may underestimate the presence of standing waters in built-up areas and densely vegetated areas due to backscattering properties of the radar signal.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/water-extents-in-mananjary-district-vatovavy-fitovinany-region-madagascar-as-of-27-februar]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: Sentinel-1 SAR imagery acquired on 27 February 2022 was processed by UNOSAT analysts using change detection techniques to identify satellite-detected surface water extents across approximately 200 km2 in Mananjary District, Madagascar, in the aftermath of Tropical Cyclone Batsirai. The resulting flood extent polygons were intersected with WorldPop population data to estimate the number of people potentially exposed to flooding. This preliminary analysis supports rapid humanitarian response and has not been field-validated.
